Gold(I) Catalysis
Room Temperature Allenation of Terminal Alkynes with Aldehydes
Junzhe Xiao, Yifan Cui+, Can Li +, Haibo Xu +, Yizhan Zhai+, Xue Zhang,* and Shengming Ma*
In memory of Dr. Ei-ichi Negishi
Abstract: A gold-catalyzed room temperature allenation of
terminal alkynes (ATA) with aldehydes affording 1,3-disub-
stituted allenes with diverse functional groups has been
developed by identifying a gold(I) catalyst and an amine.
The practicality of this reaction has been demonstrated by a ten
gram-scale synthesis and the synthetic potentials have been
demonstrated via various transformations and formal total
synthesis of (/C0)-centrolobine. Mechanistic studies revealed that
the gold catalyst, the aldehyde effect, the fluoroalkyl hydroxyl
solvent (TFE or HFIP) and the structure of amine are vital in
this room temperature ATA reaction.
Chemistry of allenes has been intensively investigated and
these elegant three-carbon units have been found to be very
powerful in organic transformations due to their unique
orthogonal cumulative p-systems,[1, 2] thus, development of
efficient methods for allene syntheses are of high current
interest. Pioneered by Crabb/C216 with paraformaldehyde and
diisopropylamine,
[3a] transition metal-mediated allenation of
terminal alkynes (ATA) reaction has been developed for such
a purpose with the scope being extended to normal aldehydes
and ketones. [3] However, there are two challenges: (1) The
reaction consists two steps: A 3-coupling reaction affording
propargylic amines and the subsequent 1,5-H transfer- b-
elimination. The rate-determining 1,5-H transfer step is of
a very high energy barrier,
[4] usually requiring reaction
temperatures of above 100 8C, which is problematic in many
cases for the relatively sensitive allene syntheses (Scheme 1).
(2) In most cases the reaction is not catalytic in metal due to
the intrinsic nature of in situ formed water and imine, which
must have reduced the catalytic performance of the metal
species. Inspired by the very limited protocols at 70
8Cb y
Hashmi[3h] and us, [3g] the gold-catalyzed 1,5-H transfer of
propargylic amines, [5] and our own understanding of the
mechanism for this transformation, herein, we wish to report
a room temperature ATA reaction affording allenes in decent
yields with a wide scope by identifying a gold(I)-carbene as
the catalyst, 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol (TFE) or 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexa-
fluoroisopropanol (HFIP) as the solvent and 1-methyl-1,2,3,4-
tetrahydroisoquinoline as the amine with the 1,5-H transfer
being mediated by the aldehyde (Scheme 1).
We started our research with benzaldehyde 1a and 1-
octyne 2a in the presence of morpholine 3a and Au(IPr)NTf
2
(Table 1). Interestingly, 18 % yield of allene 4a a was obtained
at 25 8C together with 74 % yield of the intermediate product,
propargylic amine 5 aaa. Then the effect of N-substituents in
the N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) gold complexes [6] was
screened and IMes, ICy, IAd resulted in lower yields.
Gratefully, further modification on the backbone of IPr
improved the efficiency: 27 % yield of allene 4a a and 66 %
yield of propargylic amine 5 aaa were obtained by using
Au(SIPr)NTf
2. The structure of this catalyst was established
by X-ray diffraction.
Next, we turned our attention to the effect of amines
(Table 2). Upon replacing morpholine 3a with piperidine 3b,
the yield of 4a a was improved to 41 %. Pyrrolidine 3c gave
a yield of 52 % for 4a a. When we tried 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroqui-
noline 3d , no product of 4a a was observed while the reaction
with 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline 3e [7] afforded 4a a in 19 %

droisoquinoline 3f afforded 86 % yield of 4a a with 13 % yield
of propargylic amine 5 aaf. Further screening on acyclic
secondary amines (3g to 3j ) did not give rise to better results.
Solvent effects were then carefully studied. The results
listed in T able 3 showed that fluoro-substituted alcohols were
unique for this room temperature process. Not only did 2,2,2-
trifluoroethanol (TFE) give rise to 86 % yield of 4a a,
1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) also produced
80 % yield of 4a a. In addition, 2,2,3,3,3-pentafluoropropanol
(PFP) and 2,2,3,3-tetrafluoropropanol (TFP) resulted in 71 %
and 69 % yields of 4a a, respectively. However, other fluoro-
substituted solvents without hydroxyl groups, such as C
6F6,
PhCF3, ethyl trifluoroacetate (ETFA), PhF , and non-fluoro-
substituted alcohols such as MeOH, tBuOH, EtOH, iPrOH,
afforded 4a a in less than 10 % yields. Other commonly used
organic solvents, such as DMSO, n-Hexane, Toluene, MeCN,
DMPU, DMF , NMP , MTBE, Dioxane, THF , DMC, DCM,
DCE, were poor for this reaction. Furthermore, When TFE
was compared to ethanol, trifluoromethyl moiety remarkably
promoted the A
3-coupling reaction. The ATA reaction with
ethyl trifluoroacetate (ETFA) resulted in only 6 % yield of
allene 4a a with 92 % yield of propargylic amine 5 aaf.
However, when 2 equiv of 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol were
added, the yield of allene 4a a was improved into 65 %,
indicating that the hydroxyl group must also have mediated
the rate-determining 1,5-H transfer step.
Lastly, Cu, Zn, Cd-based metal salts were examined: the
formation of allene 4a a was essentially not observed with the
reaction stopped at the stage of propargylic amine 5 aaf,
indicating that gold was irreplaceable in promoting the room
temperature 1,5-H transfer (Table 4).
With the optimized condition in hand, we turned our
attention to the scope of this room temperature ATA reaction
(Table 5). When benzaldehyde 1a (R
1 = Ph) was used,
terminal alkynes with linear alkyl, cyclopropyl, Bn, and Ph

with good yields. V arious functional groups, including halides

within aromatic aldehyde 1. To our delight, aryl aldehyde may
also accommodate useful boronate unit ( 1k ) and functional-
ized allenes with vinyl ( 4k g), halides ( 4k h, 4k i), OTBS ( 4k j),
hydroxyl ( 4k k), cyano ( 4k l), and ester ( 4k m) groups were
afforded in high yields. In addition, hetero-aryl groups ( 4l n–
4q o) commonly observed in bioactive molecules and fused
aryl groups such as naphthyl ( 4r g), phenanthrenyl ( 4s g), and
pyrenyl ( 4t g) were also viable. Even the much less reactive
aliphatic aldehyde 1u (R1 = n-C8H17) produced 27 % yield of
4u a under 25 8C for 48 h. The yield of 4u a was then improved
to 83 % by conducting the reaction under 60 8C. A series of
aliphatic aldehydes (R 1 = n-C8H17, n-C5H11, i-Bu, Cy) also
worked to afford 1,3-dialkyl- and 1-alkyl-3-aryl-disubstituted
allenes 4u a–4x a and 4u e–4x e. The practicality was also
demonstrated by applying 50 mmol of 2m (R2 =
(CH2)3CO2Me), 90 mmol of 1k (R1 = 4-(4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-
1,3,2-dioxaborolan-2-yl)phenyl), 60 mmol of 3f , and
2.5 mol % Au(SIPr)NTf 2, affording 11.0 g of 4k m in 64 %
yield under 25 8C for 48 h.
To demonstrate the superiority of this room temperature
protocol, we made a comparison between this room temper-
ature ATA reaction and the previous protocol mediated by
stoichiometric ZnI
2.[3c] For various useful functional group
substituted allenes (4c q–4i b), this room temperature protocol
improved the yields over 20 %. Especially, for sensitive
heteroaryl aldehyde, the yield of allene 4o q was improved
to 86 % from 30 % (the last part in Table 5).
Furthermore, synthetic potentials of this reaction have
been demonstrated by synthesis of various useful compounds
(Scheme 2 a). Allene 4k m went through stepwise hydrolysis/
gold(I)-catalyzed cycloisomerization
[8] to afford d-valerolac-
tone ( E)-6 in 63 % overall yield; gold(I)-catalyzed hydration
of 4k m selectively formed allylic alcohol ( E)-7 bearing useful
aryl boronate and ester groups; Suzuki coupling between
4k m and 3-bromoquinoline afforded quinolinyl allene 8 in
75 % yield; In the presence of NH
4OAc and NaIO 4, 4k m
could be transformed to correspond boronic acid, followed by
Pd-catalyzed carbonylative coupling with PhI to afford biaryl
ketone substituted allene 9 in 58 % yield; in addition, the
reaction of 1y and 2p could produce allene 4y p in 64 % yield,
furnishing the formal total synthesis of ( /C0)-centrolobine
(Scheme 2 b).
[9]
In order to unveil the mechanism, a pair of diastereomers,
the less polar propargylic amine 5 aaf-1 and the more polar
propargylic amine 5 aaf-2, were synthesized via the corre-
sponding A 3-coupling reaction under the catalysis of
20 mol % of CuBr (Scheme 3 a). [7] The room temperature
1,5-H transfer of 5 aaf-1 was slow with 5 mol % Au(SIPr)NTf2
(Scheme 3 b, Entry 1) and further promoted by excessive
0.8 equiv of benzaldehyde 1a with the generation of an
unexpected byproduct, 4-benzyl-1-methylisoquinoline 10 af
(Scheme 3 b, Entries 2 and 3), whose structure was identified
via X-ray crystallography of 10 of, an analog of 10 af (see the

DFT calculations were carried out to show the difference
between (SIPr)Au
I and (SIPr)Cu I on the rate-determining

with similar activation energies, indicating that both hydrogen
atoms may undergo the migration, which agrees well with the
deuterium-labelling experiment. Furthermore, (SIPr)Au I
mediated 1,5-H transfer features lower activation energies
as compared to the (SIPr)Cu I-catalyzed system (Figure 1),

Based on these results, we proposed a catalytic cycle [10] as
shown in Scheme 5. Alkynyl gold species Int 1 generated from
1-octyne 2a , base, and Au(SIPr)NTf 2 would undergo 1,2-
addition with the in situ generated iminium ion 11-D.
Hydrogen atom on 3-position ( Int 2 a) and deuterium on 1-
position ( Int2 b) would transfer to the alkyne moiety to
generate alkenyl gold species Int 3 a and Int 3 b, respectively,
which were somehow mediated by aldehyde 1a and TFE. b-
Elimination of Int 3 a would afford allene 4a a and imine 13-D,
while b-elimination of Int 3 b would afford allene 4 aa-D and
imine 12. Thus, an overall 31 % D-incorporation at 3-position
of allene was detected. Enamine 14, isomerized from imine 12
and 13-D, would attack the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde
1a to afford alcohol 15. Dehydration and aromatization
would afford the by-product 1-methyl-4-benzylisoquinoline
10 af with 40 % of D-incorporation at the benzylic position.
In summary, Au(SIPr)NTf
2 has been identified for the
room temperature gold(I)-catalyzed ATA reaction with
a wide scope to synthesize functionalized 1,3-disubstituted
allenes with 1-methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline as amine
and aldehyde as well as TFE as the mediator. Synthetic
potentials have been demonstrated and a formal synthesis of
(/C0)-centrolobine has been realized. Mechanistic study dem-
onstrated that the room temperature 1,5-H transfer must have
been promoted by the excess aldehyde and TFE or HFIP .
Further studies including the nature of the solvent effect on
such ATA reactions are being actively pursued in our
laboratory.
